title: Annotatio IV §.X: Gelasius — divina res; bread and wine substance remains; imago et similitudo
pass_a_gloss: Certainly the Sacraments, he says, which we take, of the body and blood of Christ, are a DIVINE THING, on account of which and through the same we are made partakers of the divine nature: Yet the substance and nature of Bread and Wine does not cease to be; Certainly the IMAGE AND LIKENESS OF THE BODY AND BLOOD of Christ are celebrated in the action of the Mysteries.
pass_b_english: Gelasius: the Sacraments of Christ’s body and blood that we take are a DIVINE THING — through them we share the divine nature.
Yet bread and wine do not cease to be in substance and nature; in the Mysteries’ action the IMAGE AND LIKENESS of body and blood are celebrated.
source_text: Certè Sacramenta, ait, quæ sumimus, corporis & sanguinis Christi, DIVINA RES est, propter quod & per eadem, divinæ naturæ consortes efficimur: Non tamen esse desinit substantia & natura Panis & Vini; Certè IMAGO ET SIMILITUDO CORPORIS ET SANGUINIS Christi in actione Mysteriorum celebrantur.
notes: Gelasius: divina res; imago et similitudo.
